source.title: AI agents now control part of Deepmind's compute for Gemini experiments, but recursive self-improvement remains distant
source.text: Google Deepmind uses AI agents to run experiments on their own for upcoming Gemini models. Research chief Koray Kavukcuoglu says the lab is still far from recursive self-improvement. For oversight, Deepmind intentionally leaves the agents' internal chains of thought untrained so they can be reviewed. Kavukcuoglu measures AGI by everyday user trust rather than benchmarks. The article AI agents now control part of Deepmind's compute for Gemini experiments, but recursive self-improvement remains distant appeared first on The Decoder .

draft.headline: Google Deepmind uses AI agents to run research experiments on upcoming Gemini models
draft.threads_post:
Google Deepmind is letting AI agents run experiments on their own for upcoming Gemini models.

Research chief Koray Kavukcuoglu says the lab is still far from recursive self-improvement. To maintain oversight, Deepmind intentionally leaves the agents' internal chains of thought untrained so reviewers can read them. He also measures AGI by everyday user trust rather than benchmarks.

Is user trust a better measure of AGI than benchmark scores?
